groups.observation: One upright triangular prism cross-section has a top vertex near x1068,y1340, a bottom-left vertex near x850,y1716 and a bottom-right vertex near x1275,y1718. The base is nearly horizontal; two straight oblique sides meet at the apex.
O is above the apex, A is below/left of the bottom-left vertex, and B is below/right of the bottom-right vertex. All three are readable.
A short interior angle arc spans the two sides immediately below the apex; φ is below that arc inside the upper part of the triangle.

A small italic n-like glyph is printed below φ. Its exact character identity is not confidently distinguishable at the original full-page observation; it must not be resolved from the author's label declaration.

Several separated groups of short oblique parallel hatch strokes are distributed inside the triangle, above and below the central ray. They are visually different from the long ray and auxiliary lines. Exact individual short-stroke count is not independently certified.
A nearly horizontal solid ray approaches from left and meets the left oblique side at about x945,y1547. A visible arrow points rightward along this approaching ray.
A solid segment continues from the left-side entry toward a right-side exit near x1200,y1588, sloping slightly down/right. A visible arrow on the interior segment points toward the exit.
The emerging solid ray leaves the right side and goes down/right outside the triangle to about x1303,y1650; its outward arrowhead is visible.

A thin straight line runs upper-left to lower-right through the left-side entry, crossing the left prism side. An angle arc lies above the approaching ray and to the left of entry between the incoming ray and the upper-left half of this normal; α is readable beside it.
A thin solid line runs lower-left to upper-right through the right-side exit, crossing the right prism side. It extends into the triangle to the lower-left and outside to the upper-right.

A broken/dashed shallow upward-right line extends from the left entry through the triangle and past the right side, ending above/right of the exit. It must not be substituted by a solid line or confused with the solid interior ray.

A second short broken oblique line runs from an interior junction on the shallow dashed line, upper-left of the exit, down/right toward the exit. It lies approximately on the backward continuation of the emerging ray.

A curved angle mark is visible above/right of the exit near the two auxiliary directions, with a readable θ to its right. At full-page scale the exact arc endpoints relative to the small dashed junctions are not independently certifiable.

The entry is on side OA and the exit on side OB, both above the base. The interior ray slopes down from entry to exit; the emerging ray turns farther down/right. The shallow dashed extension is above the exit; the two normal-like thin lines cross their respective sides at the entry/exit points. There are no numeric tick labels or grid axes.

limits.reason: The small n-like internal glyph is not an independently certain literal.
Exact tiny theta-arc endpoint geometry and individual hatch-stroke coverage are not certified by the one full-page source observation.

groups.observation: One broad ribbon/band-like object forms an upright loop with a large open circular hole. The outer curved edge reaches roughly x967..1225,y681..935; the inner hole is around x1018..1166,y739..880.

A close secondary contour follows the outer loop at the top and right, indicating a visible edge/thickness. The inner curved boundary is distinct from the outer boundary; neither should be collapsed into one circle.

A broad horizontal lower/front run extends toward the right near y879..941. The upright loop joins this run; the central open hole remains visible above it. Portions of the inner lower curve meet/are occluded by the front run.

A short straight horizontal tail extends left from the loop toward a dark end face near x870,y861..942. Several fine horizontal strand-like strokes are visible along this left tail, and the dark face has small light gaps.

The horizontal front run ends in a dark block-like right face near x1290..1304,y883..936. Short horizontal fine strokes are visible in the run near the face; a few light openings are visible in the dark end region.

Loop and ribbon boundaries are solid. No separate ray arrowhead, optical angle arc, numerical scale or grid is discernible. The two ends belong to the same coiled band appearance; they are not two unconnected loops.
No internal word, numerical label, point letter or unit is readable within the object. Its number appears only in the separate caption.

The exact individual strand/line counts and the precise tiny end-face opening shapes cannot be certified from this sole full-page source observation; do not infer a fiber count or resolve tiny gaps from an author inventory.
